bug_semantics: libsoup serializes an HTTP/1 request line by interpolating the SoupMessage method string with no escaping or token checks: write_headers() does g_string_append_printf(header, "%s %s HTTP/1.%d\r\n", soup_message_get_method(msg), uri_string, ...). soup_message_new()/soup_message_new_from_uri() and soup_message_set_method() accept any non-NULL method (including CR, LF, and other whitespace) and store it via g_intern_string. If an application feeds a user-controlled method into soup_message_new(), an attacker can inject extra header lines or a second HTTP request into the on-wire message (CWE-93 CRLF / HTTP request injection).
flaw_origin: The first write of that mechanism is Joe Shaw's 2001-06-06 commit 207f87a86eafaf04485c6e9fa077df4c250253c0. It replaced the hardcoded request-line format "POST %s HTTP/1.1\r\n" in soup_get_request_header() (libsoup/soup-queue.c) with "%s %s HTTP/1.1\r\n" interpolated from a new free-form const gchar *msg->method, and implemented soup_message_set_method() as an unvalidated assignment. The immediate parent still always sent POST and soup_message_set_method() was a stub. Later moves (soup-message-client-io.c → soup-message-io.c → soup-client-message-io-http1.c) and the 2003 soup_message_new(method, uri) API are refactors of the same unsanitized interpolation, not a new BIC.

Vulnerability first: CVE-2026-3633 is a real CWE-93 in libsoup. The attack path is an application passing a user-controlled HTTP method into soup_message_new(); that string is stored unsanitized and later interpolated into the HTTP/1 request line, so a payload such as GET
X-Injected-By: injection
 becomes extra on-wire headers or a second request. The GitHub advisory is not withdrawn; vendor trackers (Red Hat NEW, Debian unfixed, Ubuntu deferred, SUSE pending) treat it as a genuine flaw. The 2026 header-value validation for #486 is a different sink (Content-Disposition/Content-Type via soup_message_headers_append_common) and leaves the method request-line path open. " plus req->method. The parent still always sent POST. potential_fix.approach: Reject non-token HTTP methods at soup_message_set_method() (covering soup_message_new(), soup_message_new_from_uri(), and the method property): require a non-empty RFC 9110 tchar token and refuse CR, LF, SP, HTAB, and other whitespace (the same character class as is_valid_header_name() in libsoup/soup-message-headers.c). Return NULL from soup_message_new() / leave the method unset when invalid. As defense in depth, write_headers() in libsoup/http1/soup-client-message-io-http1.c must refuse to serialize if the method contains CR/LF/whitespace rather than interpolating it into the request line.
potential_fix.rationale: The injection sink is unsanitized interpolation of soup_message_get_method() into the HTTP/1 request line. Token-only methods cannot contain CRLF, so injected headers or a second request cannot be emitted even if an application forwards user input as the method. Existing header-value checks (is_valid_header_value, Closes #486) do not cover this request-line field.
